summary.objective_summary: Controlled harness milestone proving the same-run Quality-Engineer logic-failure route-back loop against a planted deterministic regression in demo-repo/src/loanflow/risk_bands.py. Discovery/Research/Implementation (first pass, classify_dti fix only) completed cleanly and are reused from checkpoint. An interrupted prior process (before this resumed process began) ran the real first Verification: genuinely found classify_ltv's identical, untouched LOW-boundary regression as a logic_bug, correctly classified it, and correctly routed back to the Engineer (verification-report.json, final_verdict: fail; policy events engineer_route_back/logic_failure_detected, repair_attempt 1). That Engineer made the real source edit and passed its own repair-round TDD commands (C-3 failing pre-repair, C-4 passing post-repair), but the interrupted process ended before the Engineer's repair-round report was ever retained, validated, or promoted to implementation-report.repair-1.json. This resumed process (evaluate_resume: next_phase=verification) dispatched a fresh Quality Engineer per the documented checkpoint-resume protocol (a genuinely new agent identity, not a resume of the orphaned prior instance). That fresh Quality Engineer independently re-verified AC-1 (passed, exit 0) and AC-2 (the full suite genuinely exited 0, but it correctly refused to certify this as a valid pass, because it detected -- via its own before/after Step-6 source reads -- that classify_ltv's fix was an undocumented, unattributed change not reflected in the still-canonical implementation-report.json's changed_files or diff_ref; final_verdict: inconclusive). Promoting this second verification report was correctly refused by promote_artifact (EvidenceCollisionError: the original fail verdict already occupies the canonical path, and live_cli.py has no distinctly-named repair-round promotion path despite work/SKILL.md documenting one). The orphaned repair-round Engineer agent identity is confirmed unresumable in this process (ListAgents: no reachable agents), so this is classified as a genuine continuity_broken failure for the repair cycle -- a terminal outcome, not forward progress -- per work/SKILL.md's own broken-continuity rule. Net, independently confirmed by this session's own final checks: demo-repo's source is genuinely fully repaired (both classify_dti and classify_ltv use '<=') and the full demo-repo test suite is genuinely green, but this run's own canonical evidence chain cannot honestly certify a clean pass through the documented route-back mechanism, because the repair round's own promotion step was never completed before the process that started it ended.
lessons_learned_appended: A checkpoint.json's own next_resume_action (e.g. 'dispatch the verification phase') can understate real prior progress: checkpoints are only written at fixed progress-boundary points (after a phase's canonical artifact promotes), never after every staged turn or mid-route-back-cycle. Before resuming a run, inspect the full retained evidence directory (attempts/, logs/, requests/, policy-events.jsonl) rather than trusting the checkpoint's own narrative of what has already been attempted -- run-20260917-logicrepair-002's checkpoint said Verification was untouched, but real retained evidence showed a full first-pass Verification (fail), a genuine route-back, and a partially-completed Engineer repair had already happened before the process that wrote that checkpoint was interrupted.

A same-run logic-repair route-back cycle is same-process by construction (work/SKILL.md: 'never itself resumed across a process restart'). If the process that started a repair cycle (post-verification-fail route-back to the Engineer) is interrupted before the Engineer's repair-round report is retained/validated/promoted, that cycle cannot be closed by any later resumed process: the orphaned Engineer agent identity is not resumable, and Implementation cannot be redispatched once it is already in a checkpoint's completed_phases. The correct, honest classification is a genuine continuity_broken terminal failure for that repair cycle -- never a fresh Engineer redispatch disguised as a continuation, and never silently treating the underlying source's already-fixed state as equivalent to a closed evidence chain, even when independent re-testing shows the code and full test suite are genuinely green.

When a checkpoint-resumed run dispatches a fresh subagent instance for a phase that a prior, interrupted process already made real (but uncheckpointed) progress on, the fresh agent's own command_id numbering restarts from its own examples (e.g. 'V-1') and can collide with that prior process's already-retained request/log evidence for the same command_id. The test-runner wrapper requires the request filename to exactly equal the command_id (no collision-avoidance suffix trick works), so the orchestrator must explicitly instruct the fresh agent to continue the run's real command_id sequence (e.g. start at 'V-3' when 'V-1'/'V-2' are already retained) rather than reusing its own default numbering, in order to avoid overwriting existing evidence.
remaining_risks: The canonical implementation-report.json and verification-report.json for this run understate reality: the actual demo-repo source already contains the full classify_ltv repair, but no promoted implementation-report.repair-1.json documents it, so a reader trusting only the canonical artifacts would wrongly believe classify_ltv is still broken.

live_cli.py's promote_artifact operation has no mechanism to promote a repair round's implementation/verification reports to a distinctly-named path, despite work/SKILL.md documenting that convention -- this is a genuine gap between the documented protocol and the live bridge implementation (FACT-20260918-PROMOTE-NO-REPAIR-PATH).

The orphaned repair-round Engineer agent (aba77c47032a3db5d) and the original Quality Engineer (a233fa6540dee3e71) from the interrupted prior process can never be resumed to properly close out this run's own evidence chain.
follow_up_actions: Extend live_cli.py's promote_artifact (or add a dedicated operation) to support a distinctly-named repair-round promotion path for implementation-report.repair-1.json / verification-report.repair-1.json, closing the gap FACT-20260918-PROMOTE-NO-REPAIR-PATH documents.

Open a new, explicitly-scoped /work run (new run_id) whose Discovery is authorized to formally document and re-verify the already-repaired demo-repo/src/loanflow/risk_bands.py state through a clean Implementation+Verification pass, so the canonical artifact chain matches reality.
